messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty PAGERDUTY-9876 triggered for service=redwood-api-canary — error-rate spike > 7% on canary cluster :rotating_light:
maya: seeing 503s on canary pods, dashboard spike at 22:10 UTC. prob related to today's deploy (release/2026-03-15). logs show image mismatch on a couple nodes.
sam: looking. which image tag was promoted? deploy-bot: promoted tag release-2026-03-15 -> registry.redwood.internal/redwood/api:release-2026-03-15
noah: canary failure started ~22:08 after automated canary rollout step 3. Reverting will impact ongoing canary metrics.
maya: grabbing pod details: `kubectl get pods -n canary -o wide` shows node1/node4 running `sha256:aa11...` but node2 shows `sha256:bb22...` (older).
olivia: that smells like a registry manifest flip/retag. we've seen 'manifest-shadowing' earlier where a mutable tag pointed at two different manifests depending on mirror consistency.
sam: running `skopeo inspect docker://registry.redwood.internal/redwood/api:release-2026-03-15` -> returned sha `sha256:aa11...` on our bastion, but on eu-mirror it's `sha256:bb22...`. mirror lag / cache-flip confirmed.
jenna: impact: ~12% of canary requests hit eu-mirror nodes -> 503s for requests expecting new entrypoints. Customer impact limited to EU canaries, not GA.
kevin: any customer-facing errors observed? SLO alerts only for internal canary route, no external pages yet, but we should prepare comms if rollback hits GA.
noah: immediate plan: 1) pause rollout, 2) toggle feature flag to stop routing traffic to canary, 3) force canary rollback to previous pinned image on cluster, 4) coordinate registry retag/immute.
maya: paused rollout via releases UI — canary pipeline stopped. toggling feature flag `feature.canary_api_v2` to off now. :white_check_mark:
noah: flag toggled. traffic back to stable. error-rate dropping.
incident-bot: Incident status -> acknowledged. assigned: sam (eng-infra), olivia (sre).
sam: starting rollback of canary pods to stable image `sha256:cc33...` with `kubectl rollout undo deployment/api-canary -n canary` — issuing now.
maya: watching pods come up. new pods with `sha256:cc33...` becoming ready. health checks passing.
olivia: deploying registry mitigation: asking registry team to set tag immutability and to re-push signed manifest for `release-2026-03-15`. also request mirror flush for eu-mirror. pinging registry team @sam.
sam: contacted registry service. they found a partial mirror promotion that rewrote the tag during a backfill job. they will: a) restore canonical manifest to primary (sha256:aa11...) b) mark tag immutable c) flush mirror caches. estimate 15-30m.
noah: do we need a kill-switch on deploy controller to prevent re-promotion? I recommend adding a temporary gating rule to block any new promotion for this release-id.
maya: added CD gating rule to block all promotions for release-2026-03-15 in the CD control plane. :lock:
sam: mirror flush started. re-pushed signed manifest to primary with signature `sig-8792`. verifying via `skopeo` on eu-mirror after flush.
jenna: monitoring metrics: canary error-rate returned to baseline within 4 minutes of flag toggle. no downstream user-facing incidents.
kevin: customer success note: emailing affected beta testers with a short FYI and that fix is in place — drafting now.
noah: next steps: 1) postmortem runbook entry, 2) add immutable-tag enforcement to CI pipeline, 3) improve registry mirror detection in canary checks, 4) add automated pre-promotion `skopeo inspect` across mirrors.
olivia: oncall handoff at 23:00 UTC -> sam will carry incident until registry mirrors fully validated. handoff notes: paused promotion, feature flag off, stable rollback complete, registry team doing immutability + flush, monitor for 1hr.
sam: ACK. I'll monitor mirrors and run synthetic tests across regions. if any divergence, I'll reroute traffic or trigger emergency rollback.
incident-bot: Incident PAGERDUTY-9876 status changed -> monitoring.
maya: quick logs for reference:
```
FAILED requests -> 503 Service Unavailable
node2 docker inspect -> manifest sha256:bb22...
node1 docker inspect -> manifest sha256:aa11...
```
noah: runbook link: https://runbooks.redwood.internal/registry/manifest-flip (runbook-47). please add notes and timeline.
kevin: publishing internal post on slack #general in 30m summarizing mitigation + customer touch.
jenna: marking incident for follow-up: add canary mirror checks + CI immutability checklists.
olivia: final note before handoff: no user-facing SLO breaches, canary health restored, registry team will confirm mirror convergence. if nothing changes by 23:30 UTC I'll close PAGERDUTY and file a low-sev incident for RCA.
sam: 23:05 UTC - registry confirms mirrors converged, tags immutable now. performing one last verification across eu/us apis. all good.
maya: thanks team. handing back to normal ops. closing thread in 30m unless new alerts. :tada:
